findings.detail: The graph routine indexes embeddings directly by parquet item_id, so it does not correctly implement the specified graph when IDs are the raw item identifiers used by the frozen parquet, rather than dense embedding-row indices. Out-of-range edges are silently discarded (182-183), and output embeddings/SIDs are still in unrelated row order. The stage1 producer explicitly writes item_ids.json to preserve this association.
findings.reproduction: For the minimal valid embedding matrix with two rows and train sequence IDs [100, 101], this function drops the edge entirely; main then rejects target 100 at lines 264-266. More generally a sparse/non-zero-based ID set cannot be mapped by positional indexing.
findings.correction: Load the stage1 item_ids.json, build item_id-to-row and row-to-item mappings, remap every history/target ID for graph construction and training, and export SIDs keyed/indexed according to the exact downstream item-ID contract. Validate unknown IDs explicitly instead of silently dropping edges.

findings.detail: The real entry point assumes parquet item IDs are dense zero-based embedding row indices and never reads the stage1 item_ids.json sidecar. Stage0's frozen builder casts raw ASIN identifiers to integers (build_recbole_parquet.py:158-162), while stage1 separately records the embedding row order in item_ids.json (generate_item_embedding.py:218-222). For the actual raw-ID data this target range check fails before training; even if it did not, positional SID export would be misindexed.
findings.reproduction: With embeddings shaped (N,D) and a frozen train.parquet target containing a raw ID >= N (e.g. the two-row counterexample target 100), running main raises ValueError at train_rqvae.py:266. If IDs happen to fall within range but are permuted relative to item_ids.json, exported SID row k labels the wrong item.
findings.correction: Honor item_ids.json and remap all train IDs to embedding row indices before graph construction, train-item selection, and target validation; export an item-ID-to-SID mapping in the format expected by stage3. Then smoke-test the actual frozen inputs and downstream loader.

findings.detail: The launcher hardcodes a machine-specific torchrun executable and launches four NCCL ranks unconditionally when invoked directly. This environment-specific path/device assumption prevents a portable real entrypoint run; no successful launcher execution can be inferred merely from its presence.
findings.reproduction: On a host without /home/wlia0047/ar57_scratch/wenyu/genrec_env_v2/bin/torchrun, direct execution fails in subprocess.call with FileNotFoundError before any training. On a host with fewer than four visible CUDA devices, the forced four-rank NCCL launch also fails.
findings.correction: Use the configured runtime's torchrun/PATH and validate available CUDA device count, or make launcher selection derive from the established project launcher while preserving its distributed configuration.
